import { Steps, Aside, FileTree, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A beamhop plugin is an ES module whose **default export** is a `BeamhopPlugin` object. It runs inside the relay
process, so it can do anything the relay can: decide which events are stored, change what readers see, check
uploads, serve HTTP, run background jobs and add pages to the admin panel.

This page builds a tiny plugin first, then tours [`plugins/hello`](https://github.com/beamhop/relay/tree/main/plugins/hello),
the example that uses every capability.

## A plugin in one file

<Steps>

1. Create `plugins/word-guard.ts` next to your config file. A single file in the plugins directory is a valid plugin.

   ```ts title="plugins/word-guard.ts"
   import { z } from "zod";
   import type { BeamhopPlugin } from "@beamhop/sdk";

   const Settings = z.object({
     word: z.string().default("spam").describe("Reject notes containing this word"),
   });

   const plugin: BeamhopPlugin<typeof Settings> = {
     name: "word-guard",
     version: "1.0.0",
     description: "Rejects notes containing a word",
     settings: Settings,
     async setup(ctx) {
       ctx.hooks.onWrite((event) => {
         if (event.content.includes(ctx.settings.get().word)) {
           return { action: "reject", reason: "blocked: bad word" };
         }
       });
     },
   };

   export default plugin;
   ```

2. Restart beamhop. Plugins are discovered and imported at boot. The default plugins directory is `./plugins`
   (`plugins.dir`, or `BEAMHOP_PLUGINS_DIR`).

3. Open **Admin → Plugins**, find `word-guard` and enable it. `setup()` runs right away; no restart needed.

4. Change the word in the plugin's settings form. The next event is checked against the new value, because the hook
   calls `ctx.settings.get()` each time.

</Steps>

<Aside type="note" title="definePlugin">
`@beamhop/sdk` also exports `definePlugin(plugin)`, which returns its argument and only helps type inference. It's
a runtime import, though. The first-party plugins use `import type` only, so they run without resolving the SDK
package at runtime — a good default.
</Aside>

## Where plugins are loaded from

| Source | Example |
| --- | --- |
| A subfolder of `plugins.dir` | `plugins/my-plugin/package.json` plus its entry |
| A single file in `plugins.dir` | `plugins/my-plugin.ts` |
| Packages listed in `plugins.packages` / `BEAMHOP_PLUGINS` | `"packages": ["beamhop-plugin-foo"]` |
| npm auto-discovery (off by default) | every `beamhop-plugin-*` or `@scope/beamhop-plugin-*` in `node_modules`, with `plugins.autoDiscoverNpm: true` |

For a folder, the entry is resolved in this order: `package.json` → `"beamhop": { "entry": "…" }`, then `main`,
`exports`, `module`, and finally `index.ts`, `index.js`, `index.mjs`, `src/index.ts`, `src/index.js` or
`dist/index.js`. Folders whose names start with `_` or `.` are skipped.

The plugin's `name` must be URL-safe (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, starting with a letter or digit): it becomes
part of route paths and the admin UI.

<Aside type="caution" title="Plugins are trusted code">
Plugins are **not sandboxed**. Every discovered module is imported at boot (so its top-level code runs even while
disabled), and an enabled plugin has full database access, the key-value store, `process.env` and the filesystem.
`ctx.config` has the obvious secrets removed, but that is hygiene, not isolation. Only install plugins you trust,
and keep side effects inside `setup()`.
</Aside>

## Bun or Node

On Bun, any TypeScript works. On Node (22.18 or newer), `.ts` entries outside `node_modules` run through type
stripping, which only supports *erasable* TypeScript:

- no `enum`, no parameter properties, no `namespace`;
- `import type` for types;
- explicit `.ts` extensions on relative imports.

Plugins published to npm should ship compiled `.js`.

## Tour of `plugins/hello`

`hello` is the reference plugin. Copy it to start a real one.

<FileTree>
- plugins/hello/
  - package.json      `main: ./src/index.ts`, script `build:ui`
  - src/
    - index.ts        the plugin
  - ui/
    - host.ts         reads React from the admin panel
    - index.tsx       admin page, dashboard widget, user action
    - tsconfig.json   JSX compiled to `h(...)`
  - dist/
    - ui.js           built admin UI bundle
</FileTree>

### The plugin object

```ts title="plugins/hello/src/index.ts (shape)"
import { z } from "zod";
import type { BeamhopPlugin, NostrEvent } from "@beamhop/sdk";

const Settings = z.object({
  blockedWord: z.string().default("forbidden-word").describe("Reject events containing this word"),
  greeting: z.string().default("Hello from beamhop!").describe("Greeting served at /plugins/hello/"),
  maxQueryLimit: z.number().int().min(1).max(5000).default(500).describe("Clamp REQ filter limits"),
  hiddenKinds: z.array(z.number().int()).default([]).describe("Kinds hidden from REQ results"),
  tickSeconds: z.number().int().min(5).default(60).describe("Heartbeat job interval"),
});

const plugin: BeamhopPlugin<typeof Settings> = {
  name: "hello",
  version: "0.1.0",
  description: "Example plugin: word filter, query clamp, routes, job, metrics and an admin page.",
  settings: Settings,
  migrations: [/* … */],
  ui: "./dist/ui.js",
  async setup(ctx) { /* … */ },
  async teardown() { /* … */ },
};

export default plugin;
```

Every field has a `.default()`, so a freshly enabled plugin starts with valid settings.

### What `setup()` registers

Each of these is covered on its own page; here is how `hello` uses them.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Hooks">

```ts
// write hook: reject a configurable word
ctx.hooks.onWrite((event: NostrEvent) => {
  const word = settings.get().blockedWord.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!word || !event.content.toLowerCase().includes(word)) return undefined;
  rejectedCounter.add(1, { kind: String(event.kind) });
  return { action: "reject", reason: `blocked: contains a forbidden word` };
});

// query hook: clamp limits
ctx.hooks.onQuery((filters) => {
  const max = settings.get().maxQueryLimit;
  if (!filters.some((f) => (f.limit ?? 0) > max)) return undefined;
  return filters.map((f) => (f.limit !== undefined && f.limit > max ? { ...f, limit: max } : f));
});

// visibility hook: hide kinds from readers (must be sync & fast)
ctx.hooks.onVisibility((event) => !settings.get().hiddenKinds.includes(event.kind));
```

See [Hooks](/relay/build/plugin-hooks/).

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Routes">

```ts
// public: /plugins/hello/ and /plugins/hello/ping
ctx.http.get("/", (c) => c.json({ greeting: settings.get().greeting, relay: ctx.runtimeSettings().info.name, seen, rejected }));
ctx.http.get("/ping", (c) => c.text("pong"));

// admin only: /admin/api/plugins/x/hello/stats and /reset
ctx.adminHttp.get("/stats", async (c) => {
  await flush();
  const recent = await db.all("SELECT id, pubkey, at, reason FROM plugin_hello_rejections ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 20");
  return c.json({ seen, rejected, recent });
});
```

See [HTTP routes](/relay/build/plugin-routes/).

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Jobs, events, metrics">

```ts
const rejectedCounter = ctx.metrics.counter("hello_rejected_total", "events rejected by the hello plugin");
const seenGauge = ctx.metrics.gauge("hello_events_seen", "accepted events observed since the plugin started");

ctx.on("event.accepted", () => {
  seen++;
  seenGauge.set(seen);
});

const stopFlush = ctx.jobs.every("flush-rejections", 5_000, flush);
```

See [Jobs, events and metrics](/relay/build/plugin-jobs-metrics/).

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Settings changes">

```ts
const startJob = (s: HelloSettings) =>
  ctx.jobs.every("heartbeat", s.tickSeconds * 1000, () => logger.debug("heartbeat", { seen, rejected }));
let stopJob = startJob(settings.get());
const offSettings = settings.onChange((s) => {
  stopJob();
  stopJob = startJob(s);
});
```

See [Settings](/relay/build/plugin-settings/).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### A pattern worth copying: buffer, then write

`hello` logs rejected events to its own table. Writing a row per rejection would put a database write on the
publish path for every spam event, so it buffers rejections in memory and a job writes them in one transaction every
5 seconds. The table is capped at 1000 rows because anonymous writers fill it.

```ts
const flush = async () => {
  if (!pending.length) return;
  const batch = pending;
  pending = [];
  await db.tx(async (tx) => {
    for (const r of batch) {
      await tx.run("INSERT INTO plugin_hello_rejections (id, pubkey, at, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING", [r.id, r.pubkey, r.at, r.reason]);
    }
    await tx.run(
      "DELETE FROM plugin_hello_rejections WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM plugin_hello_rejections ORDER BY at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?)",
      [MAX_REJECTION_ROWS],
    );
  });
};
```

### Teardown

Hooks, routes, jobs, bus listeners and settings listeners are removed by the host when the plugin is disabled.
`teardown()` is only for things you created yourself. `hello` uses it to write what is still buffered:

```ts
async teardown() {
  const fn = teardownFn;
  teardownFn = undefined;
  await fn?.(); // stops its jobs and flushes the buffer
},
```
